title: Restore ownership and verify actual access
goal: Recover a private file for its intended disposable user.
challenge: Use the supplied ll-b6 fixture. Restore separately and prove the intended account can read alpha while another identity cannot read the private restored file. Correct ownership/mode narrowly, preserve originals and explain privileged identity switching is not login authentication.

steps.command: w=/home/learner/ll-backup-6; test "$(id -un)" = learner && test ! -e "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && mkdir -m 0700 -- "$w" && cd -- "$w" && saved_umask=$(umask) && umask 077 && test "$(df -Pk . | awk 'NR==2 {print $4}')" -ge 65536
steps.explanation: Guard a fresh, learner-owned workspace and check guest free space. Stop if any command fails. Use a private practice-shell umask; restore the saved value during cleanup.
steps.expected: Private practice directory; at least 65536 KiB available.

steps.command: guard() { test "$(pwd -P)" = /home/learner/ll-backup-6 && test ! -L /home/learner/ll-backup-6 && test "$(stat -c %U .)" = learner && test -z "$(find . -type l -print -quit)"; }; guard
steps.explanation: Define and use a location/owner guard for every later change.
steps.expected: Exact physical path, not a link.

steps.command: guard && mkdir -m 0700 source && printf 'alpha\n' > source/note.txt && printf 'bravo\n' > 'source/space name.txt' && chmod 0640 source/note.txt && chmod 0600 'source/space name.txt' && touch -d '2026-01-01 00:00:00 UTC' source/note.txt 'source/space name.txt'
steps.explanation: Create two known regular files, including a name with a space.
steps.expected: alpha and bravo lines, modes640/600, fixed UTC timestamp.

steps.command: guard && ! getent passwd ll-b6 && ! getent group ll-b6 && sudo useradd -M -U -s /usr/sbin/nologin ll-b6 && sudo passwd -S ll-b6
steps.explanation: Create a locked, non-login disposable account only; do not change learner or sudoers.
steps.expected: ll-b6 password locked, no home or login.

steps.command: guard && test ! -e v1.tar && test ! -L v1.tar && chmod 0711 . source && sudo chown ll-b6:ll-b6 source/note.txt && sudo chmod 0600 source/note.txt && sudo timeout -k 1s 10s tar -cf v1.tar -C source -- note.txt && sudo chown learner:learner v1.tar && sudo chmod 0600 v1.tar && mkdir -m 0711 restore && timeout -k 1s 10s tar -xf v1.tar -C restore --no-same-owner --same-permissions
steps.explanation: Root reads the known private source for backup. Learner extraction deliberately does not restore ownership; no system destinations. Refuse existing backup/reference names before changing source or writing an archive.

steps.command: guard && sudo runuser -u ll-b6 -- cat restore/note.txt; printf 'wrong owner status=%s\n' "$?"; stat -c '%U:%G %a' restore/note.txt
steps.explanation: Actual account test detects ownership fault; root reading would hide it.

steps.command: guard && sudo chown ll-b6:ll-b6 restore/note.txt && sudo chmod 0600 restore/note.txt && sudo runuser -u ll-b6 -- cat restore/note.txt; cat restore/note.txt; printf 'learner status=%s\n' "$?"; sudo cmp -- source/note.txt restore/note.txt
steps.explanation: Restore known owner/group and private mode; verify as actual user and wrong user. Parent traversal0711 permits known-file access, not listing.
steps.expected: ll-b6 reads alpha; learner denied; sudo cmp status0. Backups/references remain private, not world-readable.

hints: Root access is not evidence of ll-b6 access.
No chmod777 or authentication changes; runuser is privileged switching.
review: Locked account, before/after actual identity reads, owner:group600 and matching payload.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 103.3 and LPIC-2 v4.5 206.2 partial manual archives/recovery; 104.5 reinforcement where applicable. Self-reviewed, unscored; not complete objectives.
